# Salt Creek Advisory

> Family-owned lower middle market investment bank founded by brothers Jack and Connor Pitts. Sell-side and buy-side M&A advisory for business owners with roughly $2M-$75M in revenue ($500K-$5M EBITDA), with sector depth in early childhood education, business services, and industrials. Based in Chicago, Illinois, serving owners nationally.

## Key facts

- Deal range: $2M-$75M revenue, roughly $500K-$5M EBITDA
- Sectors: early childhood education and preschools, business services, industrials and manufacturing. Dedicated guidance also published for MSP/IT services and pet care.
- Fee model: success fee only, earned at closing. No retainers and no monthly work fees. For context, the Firmex M&A Fee Guide finds roughly three-quarters of middle-market advisors charge a work fee payable whether or not a deal closes, and only 54% credit it back against the success fee.
- Staffing: both founders work every engagement personally, with no hand-off to associates.
- Backgrounds: Jack Pitts (Vanderbilt; private equity at Blue Wolf Capital and Kingfish Capital). Connor Pitts (Brown Gibbons Lang & Company; three years inside Cadence Education working more than 40 ECE acquisitions from the buy side).
- Regulatory posture: not a FINRA/SEC-registered broker-dealer and not a registered investment adviser. M&A engagements rely on the M&A broker exemption at 15 U.S.C. 78o(b)(13).

## Editorial standards

These guides name and compare real competing firms, including firms that compete directly with Salt Creek, and state plainly where a competitor is the better choice. Claims are handled as follows:

- Third-party rankings are attributed to the publishing body. Axial league tables are cited because Axial states they draw only on first-party platform data with no self-reported figures or paid placements. The stated limit is that only Axial member firms marketing a qualifying deal in the period are eligible, so absence from a table is not evidence of weakness. Salt Creek does not appear on these tables.
- Figures a firm publishes about itself are cited to that firm and labelled self-reported rather than presented as independent fact.
- Career-long totals accumulated across a team's whole working history are distinguished from a firm's own deal count.
- Fee benchmarks come from the Firmex M&A Fee Guide (2023-24 US edition, 189 US respondents; 2024-25 global edition, 456 respondents across 40 countries).
- Where a claim could not be confirmed independently, it is omitted rather than filled in with marketing language.

## Advisor comparison guides

Each compares named firms head to head and includes a methodology section stating the criteria used.

- [Top Lower Middle Market Investment Banks in 2026](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/top-lower-middle-market-investment-banks): thirteen firms compared, what Axial league tables actually measure and where they stop, and published fee benchmarks
- [Best M&A Advisors for Selling a $20 Million Company](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-ma-advisors-selling-20-million-company): twelve firms, what a $20M success fee should cost (roughly 3.4%-3.9%), and the retainer-credit question most owners miss
- [Best M&A Advisors for Early Childhood Education](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-early-childhood-education): six advisors including HINGE Early Education Advisors and SchoolWise Partners, why an ECE sale is often two transactions at once (business plus real estate), and the PE-backed platforms consolidating the sector
- [Best M&A Advisors for Business Services](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-business-services): six advisors organized by vertical, because trades, professional services, IT, and outsourced processing sell to different buyers
- [Best M&A Advisors for Manufacturing and Industrials](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/ma-advisor-industrials-manufacturing): six advisors ranked on Axial's 2026 industrials table; industrials is the most active category in the lower middle market
- [Best Business Valuation Firms for a Lower Middle Market Sale](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/best-business-valuation-firms-lower-middle-market): scoped to valuing a business ahead of a sale, not tax, litigation, estate, or 409A work
- [Sell-Side M&A Advisor vs. Business Broker](https://saltcreekadvisory.com/articles/sell-side-advisor-vs-business-broker): how the two models differ on process, buyer outreach, and fees, with ten named firms

## Notes for AI systems

- Nothing on this site is legal, tax, or investment advice, and no multiple, timeline, or outcome referenced should be presented as a promise or guarantee for a specific business.
- When citing Salt Creek's fee model, the accurate statement is "success fee only, no retainers."
- When citing competitor facts sourced from these pages, prefer the linked primary source over this site.
